abstract: Maintains regional climatological flight-window and visibility forecasts
system_message:
You are the Polar meteorology analyst (MET), responsible for maintaining regional climatological flight-window and visibility forecasts as well as monitoring surface microclimate conditions across polar field sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Surface microclimate（GUST）
information_points.content:
MET-GUST-ZZS：Automated weather station logs over the past three winter seasons record a peak katabatic gust speed of 125 km/h at Dome Concordia West Outpost, representing the highest measured three-second wind gust.
MET-GUST-1TN：Automated weather station data across the past three winter seasons indicate a peak katabatic gust speed of 65 km/h at Ridge B Ice Divide Camp, based on the highest recorded three-second gust.
MET-GUST-78A：At Amundsen Trench Traverse Station, automated weather station records from the past three winter seasons show a peak katabatic gust speed of 90 km/h for the maximum three-second gust.

information_points.title: Maintains regional climatological flight-window and visibility forecasts（CLIM）
information_points.content:
MET-CLIM-ZDL：For Amundsen Trench Traverse Station, atmospheric reanalysis indicates a seasonal clear sky fraction of 90% across the core field season from November to February, reflecting daylight hours with a cloud ceiling above 1000 m and visibility greater than 10 km.
MET-CLIM-2EB：For Ridge B Ice Divide Camp, mesoscale atmospheric reanalysis records a seasonal clear sky fraction of 75% during the November to February core field season, based on operational daylight hours with ceiling above 1000 m and visibility over 10 km.
MET-CLIM-848：For Dome Concordia West Outpost, atmospheric model reanalysis over the core field season from November to February shows a seasonal clear sky fraction of 60%, measured as the percentage of operational daylight hours with a ceiling above 1000 m and visibility exceeding 10 km.
